key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence images can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade, separating interface-driven failure from bulk degradation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic tool for designing more durable perovskite devices and for evaluating passivation strategies at the right failure sites.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optical signals
Bayesian inference to generate spatial parameter maps and track changes during aging
evidence_signal: The paper tracks inferred parameter maps during accelerated aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and finds strong spatially non-uniform degradation, especially at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: Inference quality depends on the fidelity of the drift-diffusion model and imaging data, so parameter maps may be sensitive to modeling assumptions and measurement noise.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
